Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Sep 08, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.  

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities. 

Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 8, 2026. 

Changes to October payment cycles: 

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.    

Payment Cycle Date 

Type of Cycle 

Claim Submission Deadline for Inclusion in Payment Cycle* 

Wednesday, 9/30/26  

Last regular payment cycle before the data freeze  

Friday, 9/25/26, 5:00 AM 

Thursday, 10/1/26 

Extra payment cycle before the data freeze 

Wednesday, 9/30/26, 5:00 AM 
There will be no payment on Wednesday, October 7. 

Thursday, 10/15/26 

First payment cycle after data freeze, in upgraded system 

Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) submission: Continuous through data freeze up to Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM 

  

Portal submission: 

Before data freeze: Friday, 10/2/26, 7:59 PM 

After data freeze: Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM 

Wednesday, 10/21/26 

Regular payment cycle, in upgraded system 

Friday, 10/16/26, 5:00 AM 

  

*As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe. 

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles: 

The HealthPAS Online Portal has returned to its previous regular operating hours. Providers again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours.   

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines. 

Other system access limitations: 

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of September 8, 2026. Topics include: 

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility 
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA) 
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal 
  • Paper & fax document submissions 
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers 
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners 
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services 
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) 
  • Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) 

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.  

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 08, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that begins September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink. 

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access

Annual Tea Celebrating Deaf Culture to Take Place September 17

September 8, 2026

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: September 8, 2026

Contact: Terry Morrell 470-7668 (videophone); 711 Maine Relay

Annual Tea Celebrating Deaf Culture to Take Place September 17

The 35th annual tea and awards presentation will take place from 2 to 4 p.m. in the Hall of Flags

AUGUSTA, MAINE -In celebration of Deaf culture and the heritage of AmericanSign Language (ASL), as well as Deaf literature, art and folklore, Governor Janet Mills has issued a proclamation designating the week of Sept. 20-26, 2026, as Deaf Culture Week.

To kick off the week, the Commission for the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened will hold its 35th Annual Tea in Celebration of Deaf Culture Week on Sept. 17, from 2 to 4 p.m. at the Hall of Flags in the State House in Augusta. The event is open to the public.

Clayton Marr III will give the keynote address. Marr grew up in Westbrook and currently lives in Knoxville, Tenn. where he is the student activity coordinator for the Tennessee Schools for the Deaf. He works with Deaf students to support their academic success, personal growth, and independence.

"Maine's Deaf community has enriched our state for generations through its language, culture, traditions and contributions. I've proudly declared September 20-26 as Deaf Culture Week in celebration of that heritage and the Deaf and hard-of-hearing Mainers who make our state a better place," said Governor Mills.

"The Maine Department of Labor is proud to support the Commission for the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened and this 35th annual celebration of Deaf culture. I encourage Maine employers to harness the many skills and experiences of people with disabilities. DOL's Bureau of Rehabilitation Services is ready to assist workers and employers with vocational rehabilitation, training and support," said Commissioner Laura Fortman.

This year, the Commission will present seven awards to eight individuals and organizations that have contributed to Deaf culture in Maine.

Awards and their recipients are:

Promoting American Sign Language, Deaf Culture and Deaf People Award Lisa Penney, Donna Van Horn

Citizenship Youth Award Gavin Phelan

Ginny Hewes Advocate for the Needs of the Deaf Community Award Jennifer McCann, LCSW

Outstanding Citizenship Award Andrew Blethen

Outstanding Commendation Award Immigrant Legal Advocacy Project (ILAP)

Dr. Toni H. Rees Interpreter Award Cid Pollard

Clifton F. Rodgers Outstanding Service to the Deaf Community Award Sammy Hargis

The Division of the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened, within the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services in the Maine Department of Labor, works to promote full access to employment, independence and community integration for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

Temporary Changes to Referral and Authorization Processes Ending November 30, 2026

Sep 08, 2026

Beginning December 1, 2026, the Department will require members to complete a Single Assessment within the past 12 months before processing referrals, prior authorization requests, and continued stay reviews for children’s medium- and high-intensity services. 

As previously communicated, the Department temporarily reinstated direct-to-provider referral and prior authorization processes while operational challenges with the Single Assessment process were being addressed. That temporary process will end November 30, 2026. 

The Single Assessment process has stabilized significantly, with assessments now completed in an average of 7.5 business days after a request is submitted. 

Thank you for your continued partnership with the Single Assessment process.

Maine Heads to The Big E with Food, Farms, and Makers

September 3, 2026

The Maine Building at the Big E returns for 17 days of Maine food, farms, makers, and traditions, September 18 - October 4

AUGUSTA, Maine (September 3, 2026) - From loaded Maine baked potatoes and lobster rolls to wild blueberry crisp, maple milkshakes, smoked salmon, and wood-fired pizza featuring Maine ingredients, the tastes and traditions of Maine are returning to The Big E this fall.

The State of Maine Building, located on the Avenue of States alongside buildings representing the five other New England states, will welcome visitors throughout the 17-day Eastern States Exposition, September 18 through October 4, 2026, in West Springfield, Massachusetts. Maine Day will be celebrated on Saturday, September 19.

For more than a century, the Maine Building has introduced generations of fairgoers to the people, products, and traditions that make Maine stand apart. The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) owns and operates the building as a showcase for Maine agriculture, food, fisheries, forests, tourism, artisans, and businesses.

"The Big E gives Maine a special opportunity to showcase our food, farms, and agricultural businesses to people from across New England and beyond," said DACF Commissioner Amanda Beal. "Food is one of the most immediate and memorable ways to make that connection. Someone may come into the Maine Building for a baked potato, lobster roll, or a maple or wild blueberry dish, but they leave with a greater appreciation for the farmers, producers, and small businesses behind those products."

The Big E is one of the largest fairs in North America, providing Maine businesses with access to an enormous regional marketplace. For exhibiting producers and makers, the opportunity extends beyond sales during the fair, helping introduce their products to new customers and build awareness that can lead to future visits, online purchases, and other business opportunities.

"We view the Big E as both a marketplace and a long-term opportunity to build awareness of Maine agriculture," said DACF Bureau of Agriculture, Food and Rural Resources Director Craig Lapine. "Many of Maine's farms and food businesses are small businesses, and reaching an audience of this scale is difficult to accomplish individually. By bringing them together in the Maine Building, we can show visitors the robust diversity of what Maine grows, harvests, makes and creates."

Taste Maine at The Big E

Food remains one of the biggest draws at the Maine Building, and the 2026 lineup offers fairgoers plenty of ways to experience Maine.

Longtime favorites include the Maine Potato Board's iconic loaded baked potatoes and Maine lobster rolls. Tree of Life Maple Farm will offer organic Maine maple syrup, maple cream, candy, cotton candy, coffee, and milkshakes, while Valley View Orchard Pies brings fruit pies, whoopie pies, and other baked goods from its Oxford bakery.

Maine aquaculture is also on the menu, with the Maine Aquaculture Association offering smoked salmon while introducing visitors to Maine's growing aquaculture sector and the Maine Oyster Trail.

This year's offerings also highlight collaborations among Maine farms and food businesses.

Fields Fields Blueberries, a woman-owned organic wild blueberry farm in Dresden, will serve its renowned wild blueberry crisp topped with Maine-made Gifford's ice cream.

QP Burger Food Truck will bring together products from multiple Maine businesses in its burgers, hot dogs, and sides, including Fox Family Potato Chips, Raye's Mustard, and Morse's sauerkraut.

Fire & Company Catering will showcase Maine flavors through wood-fired pizza and beverages featuring Maine producers and ingredients.

"These collaborations tell an important story about Maine's food economy," Beal said. "When Maine farms, food producers, and businesses use and promote one another's products, the benefit reaches beyond a single business. Visitors get a great Maine experience while seeing firsthand how interconnected our agricultural and food community can be."

More Than Food

The Maine Building experience extends well beyond the menu.

Visitors can shop for Maine-made wood products, jewelry, personal-care products, artisan goods, and gifts. Dailey Woodworking and Friends will feature work from more than a dozen Maine makers, alongside longtime and returning exhibitors including Ledgeway Farm, MARTINI Jewels, Sider's Woodcrafting, Sunshine Apothecary, and Winter Whimsies.

Short-term exhibitors rotating through the building include Maine authors and makers, Liberty Graphics, Pussums Cat Company, Sweet Monkey Business, and West Maquoit Vinegar Works.

The Maine Flower Collective will greet visitors with a display of Maine-grown dried flowers highlighting the state's flower farmers and florists, while the Maine Forest and Logging Museum will help tell the story of Maine's forestry heritage.

The Maine Office of Tourism will also be on hand, along with the Maine Tourism Association, to help visitors discover Maine destinations and experiences.

"Our goal is to spark a connection with Maine that inspires a visit to our state for culinary experiences," said Maine Office of Tourism Director Carolann Ouellette. "The Maine-made products on exhibit at the Big E all tell a story that is shaped by the landscape and culture of Maine. When fair attendees discover a Maine product, they get to learn about the farm and people behind the product, and that develops a bond that we hope will carry forward in a trip to Maine's farms and food businesses.

entry.title: US Department of Labor unveils agency-wide initiatives supporting American workers, job creators, retirees
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced its latest round of opinion letters and ongoing policy efforts to provide greater guidance and transparency to support American workers, job creators, and retirees.“This Labor Day, the Department of Labor is providing all of its stakeholders with greater clarity on federal labor laws,” said Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “This Administration is committed to clear, practical compliance assistance that helps workers understand their rights, helps employers understand their obligations, and gives all stakeholders the certainty they need to comply with the law. In honor of Labor Day, 10 agencies across the Department of Labor are delivering on that commitment.”Learn more about the department’s initiatives on the Labor Day 2026 page.Center For Faith:The department’s Center for Faith created a resource to answer common questions that faith-based organizations have regarding federal wage and hour laws. Employee Benefits Security Administration: EBSA issued an advisory opinion considering whether the Blue and Gold Automotive Health Trust Fund Welfare Benefit Plan constitutes a viable association health plan under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act such that the employers involved can band together to obtain more favorable healthcare pricing options for their employees. EBSA also published a field assistance bulletin outlining the guiding principles for EBSA’s enforcement policy regarding the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act to focus resources on areas that will have the greatest impact on access to mental health and substance use disorder benefits.Employment and Training Administration:ETA released a Training and Employment Notice 05-26, establishing a five-component framework for effective pre-apprenticeships. By strengthening pre-apprenticeship programs and giving employers the guidance and tools necessary to funnel younger workers into registered apprenticeship programs, the Trump Administration is ensuring the American workforce gains and maintains the skills necessary to build the modern and future economy. ETA also issued Circular 2026-04, informing employers that sponsor registered apprentices how to obtain money made available through the new Workforce Pell Grant, created by the Working Families Tax Cuts Act. By following this guidance and partnering with eligible educational institutions, employers using registered apprentices can access program flexibilities that allow businesses to grow and apprentices to build a high-paying career in their communities.ETA published Unemployment Insurance Program Letter 14-26, furthering President Trump’s directive to fight fraud by setting expectations for state workforce agencies to develop and implement plans to combat fraud in their state-level unemployment insurance systems and clarifying when states must adopt corrective action plans for failure to protect against the misuse of American’s tax dollars. Bureau of International Labor Affairs:ILAB released videos highlighting the American stories that put our workers front and center. From shrimpers on the Gulf Coast to workers in Alaska powering our critical minerals supply chains, the recordings demonstrate how unfair foreign competition driven by labor abuse undercuts U.S. industries – and what a level playing field really looks like. Each story makes it clear President Trump’s work is increasing U.S. job and wage growth, enforcing fair labor standards, and backing American workers and businesses with the tools they need to compete and win.Mine Safety and Health Administration:Aiming to achieve greater consistency of outcomes, MSHA recently centralized its negotiators into the Conference Litigation and Investigative Resources group. This new structure will streamline conferences, reduce litigation costs, and enhance agency credibility before judges, operators, and miners. This will help support the Trump administration’s reinvigoration of the American coal industry.MSHA recently launched a new, comprehensive “professionalism” training course for inspectors, as well as managers and administrative staff in the field who also interact with the public. To best protect America’s crucial mine workforce, MSHA must earn the trust of and build lasting relationships with those who work in and operate American mines. Equipping MSHA investigators with the skills to do both is essential for rebuilding American mining dominance.Office of Labor-Management Standards:OLMS issued an advisory opinion letter considering whether a newly formed union’s initial officer selection process is subject to the election protections and requirements of Title IV of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act. Occupational Safety and Health Administration:OSHA’s Voluntary Protection Programs promote effective worksite-based safety and health by recognizing employers for their achievements leading the way in creating stronger and safer worksites every day. OSHA recognizes employers and employees who have achieved exemplary occupational safety and health management systems through VPP.Wage and Hour Division: The division released three opinion letters responding to important questions on the application of the Fair Labor Standards Act: FLSA 2026-11: Whether an uncompensated 60-minute lunch break, during which employees spend six to 14 minutes walking to and from the employer’s designated break area, constitutes a bona fide meal period. FLSA 2026-12: Whether FLSA-exempt employees of a nonprofit organization may volunteer, outside of their normal work hours, to perform services for their employing organization.FLSA 2026-13: Whether the FLSA allows a restaurant supervisor who also works as a bartender to keep a portion of other employees’ tips and the extent to which he or she may participate in a tip pool.The Wage and Hour Division also updated its mobile app timesheet, now called WorkWise Timesheet, to provide streamlined tools for tracking regular work hours, breaks, overtime, and pay for both employees and employers.Office of Disability Employment Policy:ODEP unveiled the Make Work Pay Hub, a new website that helps job seekers, workers, retirees, and employers find financial planning resources for people with disabilities. The Hub features ABLE accounts, which let eligible workers save for disability-related expenses without affecting federal benefits, and Trump accounts, new tax-advantaged savings accounts for any U.S. citizen under 18.Veterans’ Employment and Training Service:VETS issued an opinion letter considering whether the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act protects employees from any retaliatory action by their employers because they engaged in USERRA-protected activity.

entry.title: Jury Scam Alert
entry.content:
Wednesday, September 9, 2026

Jury Scam Alert

 

The U.S. District Court for the District of Maine is aware of an ongoing jury scam involving fraudulent text messages and emails claiming that recipients failed to report for jury duty.  These messages falsely use the name of “Judge Nye” or other court officials. 

These messages are not from the Court.  The Court will never send a text or email threatening arrest or demanding payment for missed jury service.

Do not respond, provide personal or financial information, click links, or send payment in response to these messages.  Jury Scams can be reported to Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Supreme Judicial Court Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill and members of the Supreme Judicial Court will conduct a student-teacher town hall on Thursday, September 17, 2026, to commemorate the 239th anniversary of the signing of the U.S. Constitution.

"The Constitution is the bedrock and framework of American democracy," said Chief Justice Stanfill. entry.title: Honoring the Victims and Survivors of the September 11 Attacks
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Robert and Jackie Norton's son was waiting for them in California 25 years ago. He was about to get married, but his parents, a retired couple from Lubec, never made it to the ceremony. Their plane, American Airlines Flight 11, hit the North Tower of the World Trade Center in a horrific act of terrorism on September 11, 2001.

Katie Ward, the sister of Stephen Ward, said her brother couldn't wait to take over the big city when he moved to New York. A native of Gorham, Maine, Stephen had big plans, and he encouraged everyone to go after what they wanted and live their best lives. Stephen was working on the 101st floor of the North Tower at the World Trade Center that fateful day.

Robert Jalbert was raised in Lewiston and lived in Swampscott, Massachusetts, when he boarded United Flight 175 for a business trip to California. People described him as an easygoing guy, a good friend, and a proud father who went to church every Sunday and served as a Eucharistic Minister. His flight struck the South Tower of the World Trade Center.

Attorney Jim Roux of Portland, someone who loved hiking Mount Washington. He was also on United Flight 175. Through this Saturday, September 12th, the summit of Mount Washington will be lit by two pillars of light that will be visible from 100 miles away to honor Jim Roux and the thousands of others whose lives were cut short that day.

Commander Robert Schlegel was a devoted husband, a decorated officer, and an avid ice hockey and football player. Originally from Gray, Maine, Commander Schlegel had been awarded the Purple Heart and other medals for his career-long service in the U.S. Navy. He had been promoted just a month before he boarded American Airlines Flight 77, which was then flown into the Pentagon, killing all on board.

25 years ago, Maine and the nation were forever changed by the September 11th terrorist attacks. On this solemn anniversary, I join the Maine people in pausing to remember the nearly 3,000 souls taken from us that day, including the six beloved people from Maine. And in saluting the courageous first responders who rushed towards danger, including those heroes still living with devastating health conditions caused by exposure to toxic flames and fumes.

One of those firefighters moved to Falmouth, Maine. Kevin Hogan wasn't working on September 11, but when the first plane struck the World Trade Center, he jumped into a pickup truck, heading to Ground Zero. Through a storm of ash, he and other firefighters searched for scraps of clothing and under rubble, praying to find and return loved ones to their families. So today, we recognize first responders like Kevin, and we also thank the many servicemembers who stepped up to keep our nation safe then and in the years since.

And we thank our friends in other countries who stood by us. On September 11, more than 250 flights were forced to divert to Canada, including 38 commercial flights that touched down in Gander, Newfoundland, when more than 7,000 passengers were stranded. A local TV station put out a call to "lend a hand, do what you can," and residents opened their homes to Americans in need. Now, more than ever before, we should remember that kindness of our neighbors to the North. 

Although more than a hundred million Americans are too young to remember that dark day, today, we take a moment to remember and to honor those who perished that day, as well as the first responders who ran towards danger and stayed through the devastating aftermath, and the men and women who stepped up and who continue to step up to keep us safe.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and on behalf of the 1.4 million people of the state of Maine, we honor those who perished, those who helped, those who stood by us, 25 years ago, September 11, 2001.

entry.content:
STATE OF MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT STANDING ORDER REGARDING ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER JB-24-03 PILOT PROGRAM TO CONDITIONALLY AUTHORIZE LAW STUDENT EXTERNS TO PROVIDE PUBLIC DEFENSE SERVICES
Effective: September 4, 2026
On December 18, 2024, the Supreme Judicial Court adopted Administrative Order JB-24-03, Pilot Program to Conditionally Authorize Law Student Externs to Provide Public Defense Services. The order provides that it expires on September 5, 2026.
The Court has not determined whether to adopt the program permanently. There are, however, students enrolled in externships for the fall semester of 2026 who will be unable to participate in the externships if the order is allowed to expire.
Because it will take time to determine whether the program will be made permanent, but the Court does not wish to prevent the currently enrolled students from participating in their externships, it is hereby ORDERED that the effective term of the pilot program established by Administrative Order JB-24- 03 is extended through January 15, 2027.
The University of Maine School of Law and the organizations hosting student externs should not arrange for student externs for the spring semester of 2027 without first confirming that the pilot program will remain in effect for that semester.
Dated: September 4, 2026 For the Court:
/s/ Valerie Stanfill Chief Justice

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 14, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that began September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Sep 14, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.  

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities. 

Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 14, 2026. 

Changes to October payment cycles: 

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.

  *As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe. 

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles: 

The HealthPAS Online Portal has returned to its previous regular operating hours. Providers again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours.   

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines.

Other system access limitations:   

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of September 14, 2026. Topics include: 

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility 
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA) 
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal 
  • Paper & fax document submissions 
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers 
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners 
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services 
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) 
  • Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) 

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.   

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

entry.title: US Department of Labor debars Louisiana employer from H-2A visa program for federal violations
entry.content: NEW ORLEANS – The U.S. Department of Labor debarred a Calcasieu Parish farmer from participating in the H-2A visa program for one year, after an investigation discovered multiple violations under the H-2A program.The department’s Wage and Hour Division determined that Jevon Natali, operating as Jevon Natali Farms near Lake Charles, violated H-2A program requirements when it misrepresented the actual terms and conditions of employment on its submitted job order. The H-2A visa program allows agricultural employers who anticipate a shortage of domestic workers to bring nonimmigrant foreign workers to the U.S. to perform agricultural labor of a temporary or seasonal nature. The one-year debarment prohibits the employer from hiring workers through the program during that period because of the seriousness of the violations.“Employers who abuse the H-2A program should expect to be held accountable for their actions,” said Wage and Hour Division District Director Troy Mouton in New Orleans. “Debarment sends a clear message that the Department of Labor will protect the integrity of this program and safeguard opportunities for American workers.”Division investigators also found Fair Labor Standards Act violations when Jevon Natali Farms failed to pay the required overtime premium of time-and-one-half employees’ regular rates of payfor non-agricultural work performed over 40 hours in a workweek. Jevon Natali Farms also failed to provide paystubs with the required information.Employees and employers can contact the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division.

Many Erosion Control Certifications will be expiring for individuals at the end of December, and continuing education hours are required to keep your certification current. Please send any updates to NPSTraining.DEP@maine.gov.

The NPSTC will be offering in-person trainings statewide this fall and winter, with more being added in other locations over time.
